Plan row 1.3 asks for three things and the diff does exactly those: (1) `abs(oE2) < 1e-300` in place of `oE2 < 1e-300` (for d > 0, oE2 in (0,1] so `abs` is the identity — the mu<lam path is untouched; for d < 0, oE2 < 0 and the old guard fired on every segment, which is the mechanism H12 describes); (2) the critical branch rewritten as I_lam = lam0*dt - log(a1/a2), I_mu = lam0*dt + log((tp-t1)/(tp-t2)); (3) `.bdi_p_cr` returning the limit 1/(1 + lam0*(tp-t)) under a relative tolerance 1e-12*max(|lam0|,|mu0|), the same switch in both functions.

I re-derived both critical-branch integrals independently and they are right: with p = 1/(1+lam*tau), 1-p = lam*tau/(1+lam*tau), so lam*(1-p) = lam - lam/(1+lam*tau) giving lam*dt - log(a1/a2), and mu/(1-p) = (1+lam*tau)/tau = lam + 1/tau giving lam*dt + log(tau1/tau2). The pre-fix code had the two swapped in sign/shape (it had written 1-p where p belongs), which is exactly H54's 4.433-vs-8.143. I also re-derived the general branch (unchanged) and confirmed both identities in the roxygen block are correct and sign-safe for mu>lam (lam - mu*E and 1-E are both negative, ratios positive).

Three deviations, all declared in the fixer's report and all justified: the `n > 0L` gate on I_mu in the critical branch (without it, n=0 with t2=tp gives 0*Inf = NaN — the general branch already had this shape, so the branches are now symmetric); the DDD btorph convention (I verified with DDD 5.2.4 that fhat - bd_loglik(btorph=0) = -lgamma(n) and fhat = bd_loglik(btorph=1), so the plan row's literal wording "btorph = 1 ... = -log((n-1)!)" does not hold numerically and the fixer pinning both forms is the right call); and the worktree base-commit reset.

One undeclared consequence: the switch went from absolute (1e-15) to relative (1e-12*max), so on the mu<lam side the sliver |d| in [1e-15, 1e-12*lam) now takes the critical branch where it used to take the general one. The plan's risk column says "mu0 < lam0 path unchanged"; strictly it is unchanged only outside that sliver. The change is an improvement there (measured below), so this is a wording point, not a defect.

WHAT BROKE — two things.

(A) OVERFLOW: the fix is valid only for |lam0-mu0|*(tp-t1) < ~709. `E = exp(-d*(tp-t))` overflows on the mu>lam side, and the new comment's claim "valid for any lam0, mu0 >= 0" is false there.
  `.bdi_integral_cr(0, 3, n, 2, lam=0.1, mu=142.1, tp=5)`: -Inf for n=0, NaN for n=1 (finite and correct at mu-lam = 140). Deep-time equivalent: tp=100, mu-lam = 7.1 -> NaN.

  Mitigating: `auto_bounds(brts11, model="cr", link="exponential")` gives upper_bound 0.2576 on both log-rates (mu <= 1.29), so the default route never gets there; it needs a user-supplied box, and on the linear link it needs rates in the hundreds. Low-to-medium reachability, but the failure mode is the one under repair.

(B) NEAR-CRITICAL CANCELLATION BAND: the switch constant 1e-12 is placed at the peak of the general branch's cancellation error, not past it. Measured on the 11-tip tree, sample_size 20, lam = 0.5, varying d = lam-mu (1.3_attack_band.R):
    d = +/-1e-13 (inside the switch): range(lw) 1.9e-12 / 2.5e-12, fhat-bd 5e-12
    d = +/-1e-12 (just outside):      range(lw) 7.4e-3 / 6.8e-3, fhat-bd 2.2e-4 / 3.2e-4
    d = +/-1e-11: range(lw) ~1e-3;  1e-10: ~2e-5;  1e-8: ~5e-7;  1e-6: ~6e-9;  1e-4: ~2e-10
  So the "zero-variance / exact" property (the test's own 1e-8 bar) fails for |lam-mu|/lam roughly in [1e-12, 1e-6], worst right at the switch. Mechanism confirmed: `lam0 - mu0*E` is a cancelling difference of O(lam) numbers whose result is O(d*(1+mu*tau)); near tp the tau-weighting vanishes and the relative error is eps_mach*lam/d ~ 1e-4 at d = 1e-12, amplified by the (n+2k) multiplier and summed over segments. It is not a regression (on the mu<lam side this band behaved the same pre-fix; the fix strictly improved [1e-15, 5e-13]), but it contradicts the fixer's stated justification for the constant, which was measured on `.bdi_p_cr` alone ("exact to 1e-12 at d = 1e-13") and does not transfer to the integral or to the sampler's weights.
  Note that raising the threshold does not fix this: the limit's own error grows like d*tau while the general branch's falls like eps*lam/d, and they cross at |d| ~ 3e-8*lam with a floor of ~1e-7 relative. Only a cancellation-free formulation removes the band.

Also latent, not worth a merge block: `abs(d) <= 1e-12 * max(abs(lam0), abs(mu0))` evaluates TRUE when lam0 is Inf (exp overflow in `.bdi_lam` at link=1 with eta > 709), routing an infinite rate into the critical branch where pre-fix it took the general one. Both are nonsense; neither errors. Needs a box upper bound above ~709 on the log scale.

rule_matches_plan:
Clause by clause against plan row 1.6, the code implements the rule and I could not break the core of it.

(a) Stopping rule (H21). `rel_delta(new, old) = max_j |new_j - old_j| / pmax(|old_j|, 1e-2)`; the box never enters. Verified behaviourally: with ub = c(30,30) and c(300,300) PRE-FIX reports "converged" after 4 and 3 iterations at parameters ~0.75/0.04 and 0.78/0.11; POST-FIX the same three boxes (ub 2/1, 30/30, 300/300) all run to max_iter = 25 — the box-dependence of the verdict is gone. `abs_step` and a `patience`-window `drift` are recorded as the plan asks.
(b) Final E-step at theta_K (H20). Run at `prev_pars`, appended as a trace row with `final_estep = TRUE` and NA step columns; `last_results` is replaced so `final_IS`, `ESS` and `loglik_var` describe the returned point, and `.run_mcem`'s `tail(fhat)` rule then reports fhat(theta_K). I confirmed `final_IS$fhat == mcem$fhat[last]` exactly (E_step.cpp:165 uses the same S_completed denominator as `.is_fhat`), including a run with 1605 overrun rejections.
(c) maxN ratchet (H22). `maxN <- as.integer(max(maxN, min(2*maxN, 50000L)))` in the failure branch only, never reset on success; returned as `$maxN`. Verified: sample_size 300 / maxN 200 fails once, ratchets to 400 and stays; 8 injected failures reach the 50000 cap.
(d) Restart-then-perturb (H22/H30). fail_streak 1 -> `cur_pars <- prev_pars` (a no-op by construction, so the recovery is the larger cap alone); fail_streak >= 2 -> 0.8*cur + 0.2*centre, clamped. Strict fail/success alternation therefore never perturbs, which is exactly the drag H22 documented; `prev_pars` is never overwritten by a perturbed point, so the 0.8^8 mixture is unreachable.
(e) Streak reset (H30): `streak <- 0L` in the failure branch, before the break test.
(f) All-fail return (H31): `pars = prev_pars` (= init), `iterations = n_success = 0L`, `n_failed`, `stop_reason`, `mcem = NULL`; `.run_mcem` passes `iterations`/`stop_reason` up and `print` shows them.
(g) Rejection columns (H34): `rejected`, `rejected_overruns`, `rejected_lambda`, `rejected_zero_weights`, `n_rejected`, with `n_rejected` the same three-term sum `final_IS$n_rejected` uses.

(1) Plan row 1.5, whose stopping rule row 1.6 is told to share, also says "an iteration whose M-step returned init unchanged does not count toward patience"; `.mcem_bdi` implements that as the `m_moved` guard, `.mcem_dynamic_fresh` has no equivalent, so three no-move iterations still report "converged" with delta_max = 0 (reproduced with lower_bound == upper_bound; both builds do it, so nothing regressed, but the siblings now differ). (3) `run_em` is a full `em_cpp` call, so the "final E-step" also runs and discards an M-step (the BDI sibling calls `e_step_at` only). rule_matches_plan: The rule is implemented almost exactly as the plan row states, and it works. src/E_step.cpp:104 accepts iff `std::isfinite(log_w)` (the `0.0 < std::exp(log_w)` underflow cut is gone); :117 routes an exact `-Inf` to `rejected_zero_weights`; :122 routes everything else to the new `rejected_nonfinite`; the lock is taken at :102 BEFORE the stop test and the push, the push is guarded by `if (trees.size() < N)`, `stop` is only ever written `true` (:85, :113), the loop `break`s on stop at :74 and :103, and each catch handler re-checks stop before incrementing so nothing is counted after the sample is full; :164 uses `trees.size() + rejected_zero_weights`. `stop` was already `std::atomic<bool>` on main, so the unlocked read at :74 is not a race. rule_matches_plan:
The plan row (02-findings.md §3, wave 1, row 1.8) asks for four things: (i) start-of-interval rate from the segment's post-event count via upper_bound(cbt); (ii) a dominating envelope for monotone rates; (iii) a safety factor plus an assert pt<=1 otherwise; (iv) no collapse after a rejection.

(i) Implemented correctly, by a different but equivalent route: `segment_start_rate()` evaluates `model.nh_rate` at `std::nextafter(cbt, next_bt)`. `nh_rate` selects its node with `lower_bound_node(t)`, which for any t in (cbt, next_bt] returns the node at next_bt — the same node `upper_bound(cbt)` returns — whose `n` is the count on the segment (node_t doc: "n[i] = number of species in [time_i-1, time_i)"). The survival factor moves by one ULP. Verified by reading model.hpp:238-252 and model_helpers.hpp:118-122.

(ii) The monotonicity argument holds and I checked it independently. nh(t) = n*lambda*(1 - rho*exp(-mu_eff*(T-t))) with mu_eff = max(mu,1e-10); with the node fixed on the segment the only t-dependence is the exp factor, which is increasing in t, so nh is strictly decreasing and the start value dominates. The `constant_rates` guard `pars[2]==0 && pars[3]==0 && pars[6]==0 && pars[7]==0` is the right condition and is stricter than checking model_bin: slots 2/3 (beta_M/beta_D) and 6/7 (gamma_M/gamma_D) are the only ones through which t enters the rate (via M = calculate_pendant_pd(t)/n and D = e_s - M), and `speciation_rate()` multiplies pars[2]*M whether or not model_bin says M is active, so testing pars rather than model_bin is the correct call. Under all three links lambda and mu then depend on n only, so this covers cr, dd, and any link. Confirmed empirically: zero violations across cr (linear/exp/gaussian), mu<lambda, mu==lambda, mu>lambda, mu=0, lambda=1e-8, rho=0.5, rho=0.2, 2-tip tree, 30-tip tree, sample_size=1, num_threads=4, dd linear/exp/gaussian including a steep dd.

(iii) DEVIATION THAT MATTERS. The plan says "safety factor + assert pt <= 1 otherwise". What shipped is a safety factor of 2 and a counter — no assert, no throw, no warning, and pt is silently clipped (the clip is a behavioural no-op: u2 in [0,1) so u2 < pt was already always true for pt>=1). The factor 2 is a heuristic and it is not enough: on the D-active models (`model = "d"` / `"nd"`, the package's headline models) the counter fires at ordinary parameter values — nd/linear beta_D = -0.2 gives 7 violations per 2000 draws, -0.5 gives 11, -1.0 gives 19, -2.0 gives 33; d/gaussian beta_D = -1 gives 2; nd/exp beta_D = -2 gives 1. So the envelope still does not dominate on a supported path, and the plan row's own pinning criterion ("no pt > 1 counter hits") is not met there.

(iv) Implemented correctly. `new_interval` stays false through a rejected candidate, so lambda_max is held for the rest of the segment; it is set true only on an accepted insertion (both the insert_species and insert_unsampled_species branches) and on reaching next_bt. The pre-fix collapse to nh(next_bt) is gone. `max_lambda` is now checked only when the envelope is recomputed, which is equivalent since it cannot change otherwise.

sampling_prob and every other likelihood function are untouched, which is right — thinning yields an exact NHPP with rate nh(t) when the envelope dominates, so the density needed no change.
